test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which body emphasised safety audits for women in public spaces during a symposium in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Human Rights Commission**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• In **June 2025**, the **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** convened a significant national symposium specifically addressing the **safety and security of women** in public and semi-public spaces across India. 
 
• The commission strongly advocated for the institutionalization of **safety audits**, which are systematic evaluations of the physical and social environment of **urban spaces** to identify factors that contribute to a lack of safety for **women**. 
 
• The **NHRC** highlighted that these audits should focus on **infrastructure gaps** such as poor **street lighting**, lack of **CCTV coverage**, and inadequate **public transport** facilities that hinder women's mobility. ***Hence, the correct answer is the National Human Rights Commission.*** 
 
• The body emphasized that **urban local bodies (ULBs)** and **police departments** must collaborate with **civil society organizations** to conduct these audits periodically to ensure **gender-responsive urban planning**. 
 
• During the symposium, the **NHRC** also pointed out the necessity of **technological integration**, such as mobile-based **panic buttons** and real-time **tracking systems**, as a follow-up to the findings of the **safety audits**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):** 
 
 
• It is a **Statutory public body** established on **12 October 1993** under the **Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993**. 
 
• The commission is headquartered in **New Delhi** and serves as the watchdog of human rights in the country, relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity of the individual as guaranteed by the **Constitution of India**. 
 
• The **Chairperson** and members are appointed by the **President of India** on the recommendations of a high-powered committee headed by the **Prime Minister**. 
 
 
 
• **Safety Audits and Urban Design:** 
 
 
• A **safety audit** is a participatory tool developed originally in **Canada** in the **1980s** to involve women in the assessment of their own safety in the **urban environment**. 
 
• In India, various **NGOs** like **Jagori** and **Safetipin** have pioneered the use of safety audits to map **safety scores** for different areas in cities like **Delhi**, **Mumbai**, and **Bengaluru**. 
 
• Key parameters of these audits include **lighting**, **openness**, **visibility**, **crowd**, **security**, and **walkpath** availability. 
 
 
 
• **Safe City Project:** 
 
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** has implemented the **Safe City Project** under the **Nirbhaya Fund** in **8 major cities**: **Ahmedabad**, **Bengaluru**, **Chennai**, **Delhi**, **Hyderabad**, **Kolkata**, **Lucknow**, and **Mumbai**. 
 
• This project aligns with the **NHRC's** recommendations by focusing on **smart policing**, **emergency response systems**, and **gender-sensitization** of the police force. 
 
• It also aims at improving **forensic facilities** and establishing **One Stop Centres (OSC)** for women in distress. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Article 21** of the **Indian Constitution** guarantees the **Right to Life and Personal Liberty**, which the **NHRC** interprets to include the right to move freely and safely in public spaces without fear of **gender-based violence**. 
 
• The **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11** specifically targets making cities and human settlements **inclusive**, **safe**, **resilient**, and **sustainable**, with a focus on providing universal access to safe, inclusive, and accessible **green and public spaces**, especially for women. 
 
• **Section 12** of the **PHRA, 1993**, empowers the **NHRC** to review the factors that inhibit the enjoyment of human rights and recommend appropriate **remedial measures** to the government.
